Subject: Discovery readout + PoC hypothesis validation and onboarding checklist

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Below is a concise readout from our call, the PoC hypotheses we agreed to validate, and a pragmatic onboarding checklist so we can hit the ground running. Please confirm or flag anything missing.

1) Confirmed pain points (as stated by OptiLabs)
- 95th percentile latency for inference spikes beyond 800ms during peak batches (affects front-end UX)
- Unit cost variability (esp. during batch workloads) undermining predictable pricing for customers
- Limited production observability for token-level cost + latency breakdowns

2) Primary goals for the PoC (success criteria)
- Reduce 95th latency for the targeted prompt set to <200ms (regional EU endpoint)
- Reduce per-token serving cost by ~30% vs current baseline via batching/quantization recommendations
- Deliver visibility: per-route latency and token cost dashboards + prompt-level quality regressions tracked

3) Hypotheses we will validate in the 3-week PoC
- H1: Intelligent batching + prefix caching will yield 20-40% cost delta without breaching latency SLOs
- H2: Model quantization profiles recommended by Redwood Optimize will maintain >95% of baseline answer quality on the sample prompt set
- H3: Smart routing to an EU-dedicated pool will keep tail latency stable under production-like load patterns

4) PoC scope (what we will run)
- Duration: 3 weeks (baseline + tuning + readout)
- Volume target: 30k requests/day (sample distribution attached), ~200k tokens/day
- Models: open/Redwood-verified LLM variants (we will propose two candidate model variants in the kickoff)
- Deliverables: baseline measurements, tuning playbook, evaluation report with prompt/eval suite, runbook for production rollout

5) Owners and points of contact
- OptiLabs: Elena Morris (PM, primary), Rahul Singh (SRE/infra)
- Redwood: Marissa Cole (Account Exec, project owner), Ben Carter (Solutions Engineer lead), Karthik Iyer (Security/infra lead)

6) Timeline & milestones
- Week 0 (pre-kick): access & credentials, test dataset uploaded, security Q&A answered
- Week 1: baseline collection + small-scale tests (day 1–3), initial batching/kv-cache config (day 4–7)
- Week 2: quantization experiments and quality evals, iterate model variant (day 8–14)
- Week 3: stability runs, final readout, handoff notes and next-step recommendations (day 15–21)

7) Access / setup checklist (action items for OptiLabs)
- Provide S3 path or Share link with test corpus (expected: sample_prompts_optilabs.csv)
- Create a service account for Redwood with read-only S3 access OR provide a temporary signed URL for ingestion
- Whitelist Redwood IP ranges for EU test endpoint (we will share the list once we confirm region)
- Provide SOC2 evidence or a security contact for the questionnaire (Karthik will follow up)

Attachments: poc-charter-optilabs.pdf (PoC charter + milestones), sample_prompts_optilabs.csv (example prompt set)

Ask: Can you confirm (A) access to the test corpus by next Tuesday (Oct 20) and (B) whether an EU test endpoint is required for the entire PoC? If yes, we’ll provision EU-dedicated capacity for the trial.

Next steps from Redwood if you confirm: send DocuSign for the PoC statement of work, schedule a 30–45 minute technical kickoff with Ben & Karthik (we propose Oct 20–22), and provision initial baseline endpoint.

Thanks — looking forward to running this with you.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
